title: Add cross-run variance normalizer and soft-fail window CI adapter
author: Leah Morgan
release_notes: Adds a CI adapter that normalizes metric variance across runs and a configurable soft-fail window. No breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: CI noise and non-deterministic metric drift have caused several spurious regression blockers recently. This PR introduces a cross-run variance normalizer and a configurable soft-fail window adapter for the eval CI pipeline so small, transient variance blips do not immediately block merges while still surfacing actionable signals for on-call and triage.

What this changes: Adds a lightweight normalization layer that computes a rolling median and interquartile range (IQR) for control cohorts (anchor prompts) and normalizes incoming run metrics against that baseline. The normalized z-like score is used to compute a `variance_score` per prompt cohort. The CI adapter applies a soft-fail policy: if the aggregated variance_score is within a user-configurable grace window, the job reports as WARN (soft-fail) and triggers a deferred stochastic replay probe that runs a deterministic subset with slight perturbations; only sustained deviations outside the window cause a hard FAIL.

Key behavior details: Configuration is available via eval_harness/config/defaults.yaml with knobs: `soft_fail_threshold`, `grace_window_minutes`, `rolling_window_runs`, `control_cohorts`, and `stochastic_replay_fraction`. Baseline persistence is implemented via a small local state store (sqlite by default; S3/redis plugins are plumbed) with automatic expiry/GC for old runs. The adapter integrates with existing reporting so alerts and PR comments include both raw and normalized metrics and a short explanation of whether the CI result is a hard fail, soft-fail (deferred probe queued), or pass.

Why this approach: Normalizing against historical baseline reduces false positives from run-to-run variance (worker noise, quantization nondeterminism). The deferred stochastic replay provides higher-confidence verification without blocking developer velocity on every minor fluctuation. The design keeps defaults conservative (soft-fail on first crossing, hard fail after 2 successive windows) and is opt-in per repo via `.eval-config.yaml`.

Compatibility and rollout: Backwards compatible for projects that don't enable the adapter. We add a feature flag `EVAL_USE_VARIANCE_NORMALIZER`. On rollout we plan: enable soft-fail in shadow mode for 2 weeks (metrics-only), then enable gating with alerting, then flip to hard fail after operational tuning.

Testing and validation: Unit tests included for normalization math and baseline persistence. Integration tests run a simulated CI pipeline with seeded noise patterns to verify soft-fail -> replay -> escalation path. We measured a ~68% reduction in spurious hard fails across a 2-week noisy sample in the staging harness.

Notes: configuration examples and a short troubleshooting guide are added to docs/ci_adapters.md. The adapter emits Prometheus metrics for `eval_variance_score`, `eval_soft_fail_count`, and `eval_replay_queue_size`.
